 "new_string": "def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    from collections import Counter
    background = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    # Full solid non-background lines are the tile separators.
    row_colors = {r: grid[r][0] for r in range(h) if len(set(grid[r])) == 1 and grid[r][0] != background}
    col_colors = {c: grid[0][c] for c in range(w) if all(grid[r][c] == grid[0][c] for r in range(h)) and grid[0][c] != background}
    # Select a separator color shared by the horizontal/vertical lines if possible.
    colors = set(row_colors.values()) | set(col_colors.values())
    color = max(colors, key=lambda x: list(row_colors.values()).count(x) + list(col_colors.values()).count(x))
    hbars = [r for r, x in row_colors.items() if x == color]
    vbars = [c for c, x in col_colors.items() if x == color]
    def segments(n, bars):
        result, start = [], 0
        for b in bars:
            if start < b: result.append((start, b))
            start = b + 1
        if start < n: result.append((start, n))
        return result
    rs, cs = segments(h, hbars), segments(w, vbars)
    # The filled tile is the segment with the most non-background cells.
    candidates = [(sum(grid[r][c] != background for r in range(a,b) for c in (x,y) for y in []), a,b,x,y) for a,b in rs for x,y in cs]
    # Explicit scoring avoids any dependence on empty separators.
    candidates = [(sum(grid[r][c] != background for r in range(a,b) for c in range(x,y)), a,b,x,y) for a,b in rs for x,y in cs]
    _, a, b, x, y = max(candidates)
    tile = [row[x:y] for row in grid[a:b]]
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    for rr, (r0,r1) in enumerate(rs):
        for cc, (c0,c1) in enumerate(cs):
            for r in range(r0,r1):
                for c in range(c0,c1):
                    out[r][c] = tile[(r-r0) % len(tile)][(c-c0) % len(tile[0])]
    return out
",
